title: Gear Trains — Types & Speed Ratio
subtitle: Dr Opemibo's section starts here. Gear trains are systems of gears working together to transmit motion. You'll learn the four main types, how to calculate speed ratio, and the relationship between number of teeth and speed.
learningOutcome: Dr Opemibo's section starts here. Gear trains are systems of gears working together to transmit motion. You'll learn the four main types, how to calculate speed ratio, and the relationship between number of teeth and speed.

content.text:
Exam-ready definition (from notes):
A gear train is a mechanical system consisting of 2 or more gears used to transmit motion, speed & direction. It's all about putting gears together and each one has its own shaft.

items: 1. Simple gear train — shafts are parallel and do not intersect
2. Compound gear train — one shaft carries (shares) 2 gears
3. Reverted gear train — input and output shafts are on the same line
4. Epicyclic gear train — gears rotate around other gears (also called Planetary gear system)

content.text: Epicyclic consists of: Ring/Angular gear · Planet gears · Sun gear

items: An idler gear is placed between 2 other gears (usually driver and driven) and does NOT change the gear ratio.
It moves in opposite direction. It changes the direction of the driven gear and bridges distance between gears that are far apart.

content.text: N₁ = speed of driver gear (rpm) · N₂ = speed of driven gear (rpm) · Z₁ = number of teeth on driver · Z₂ = number of teeth on driven · High gear ratio → high torque, low speed, bigger teeth · Low gear ratio → low torque, high speed, smaller teeth

A bicycle has gears. When you shift to a small front gear and big rear gear (low gear ratio), the wheel turns slower but you can climb hills easily (high torque). When you shift to high gear, the wheel spins fast (high speed) but you need to pedal harder on hills. That's exactly what gear ratio does.
Common mistake — Students write N₁/N₂ = Z₁/Z₂ (wrong — teeth and speed are inversely proportional). More teeth = slower speed. The correct formula is N₁/N₂ = Z₂/Z₁.

items: • Define a gear train. State and describe the four types.
• Use speed ratio N₁/N₂ = Z₂/Z₁ to find unknown speeds or teeth counts.
• What is an idler gear? What does it and doesn't it change?
